dataset_info.description: Part 6 of the VEDA disease database. Covers Kushtha through Skin Diseases General. Includes all obstetric sub-entries, paediatric sub-entries, toxicology entries, full Rasayana list, and major disease entries with expanded Volume 2 herb lists. Continues from Part 5 (DIS-211 to DIS-271).

diseases.description: Broad category of chronic skin diseases including leprosy. Volume 2 significantly expands with 44 herbs including Cakramarda, Kakamaci, Karanja, Karavira, Karpasa, Katuka, Khadira, Kosataki, Krsna-vetra, Kutaja, Lakuca, Lodhra, Mamsi, Manjistha, Mulaka, Murva, Muskaka, Nimba and Mudgaparni.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Generally disease of skin and particularly leprosy (Kshudrakushtha and Mahakushtha)
A skin disease causing darkness, roughening and hardness of skin
Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases

diseases.description: A type of Kushtha characterised by white or coppery circular spots like bottle-gourd flowers on chest. Volume 2 adds Bana and Kakajangha.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: A type of Kushtha characterised by white or coppery circular spots like flowers of bottle-gourd
Generally disease of skin and particularly leprosy

diseases.description: Abnormal liver enlargement (hepatomegaly). Volume 2 adds Kalamegha (King of Bitters), Kakamaci and Kumari — strong hepatoprotective and cholagogue herbs.
General mental and psychological disorders. Volume 2 adds Girikarnika, Jyotismati, Devadaru, Kusmanda and Jatamansi to Brahmi and Mandukaparni.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Psychiatric involvement; anomalies of abnormalcy (bodily, psychosomatic or psychic)

diseases.description: Narcotic state or drug-induced stupor. Volume 2 associates Haritaki and Kustha for management.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: An intoxicating effect; intoxication, toxicating, exhilarating

diseases.description: Excess body fat accumulation from Kapha predominance and metabolic dysfunction. Volume 2 adds Atimuktaka, Babbula, Badari, Bilva, Gavedhuka, Mahatpancamula and Mundi.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Aids in reducing corpulency; act of scraping, reduction of body weight
Purification; radical elimination of morbid substances

diseases.description: Herbs for preventing miscarriage and stabilising pregnancy. Volume 2 lists Kamala, Kaseru and Nyagrodhadi gana.
Prolonged or obstructed labour with abnormal foetal position. Volume 2 adds Atibala, Bala, Bhurja and Langali.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Difficult and delayed labour; abnormal posture of foetus

diseases.description: Herbs used to accelerate or stimulate labour. Volume 2 adds Jimutaka and Langali to Godhuma.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Expulsion of placenta; delivery of foetus; obstetrics

diseases.description: Failure to expel placenta after delivery; retained placenta. Volume 2 lists Katukalabu, Langali and Kikkisa.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Expulsion of placenta (delivery of foetus); obstetrics

diseases.description: Pain during pregnancy. Volume 2 lists Bala, Draksa and Ervaru.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Colic; ache; pain; disease or symptom

diseases.description: Post-partum complications. Volume 2 adds Methika (fenugreek) for its galactagogue and uterine tonic properties.
Classical Ayurvedic ritual using specific herbs to influence the sex of the foetus during pregnancy. Lists Kantakari-Sveta and Laksmana.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Measures prescribed for reversal of sex in foetus during the pregnancy period

diseases.description: Herbs used specifically to stabilise a threatened pregnancy and prevent miscarriage. Lists Bhrngaraja, Durva and Kaseruka.
Abnormal fluid accumulation causing swelling. Volume 2 expands to 27 herbs adding Canda, Girikarnika, Karna, Karpasa, Katutumbi, Kiratatikta, Kustha, Mamsi, Manaka and Mulaka.
General children's diseases. Volume 2 lists Amalaki, Ativisa, Ardraka, Bhurja, Bilva, Brahmi, Brhati, Coraka, Hribera, Kamala, Kustha, Madhulika and Mundi.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Seizures in children causing various syndromes (Grahavadha, Bhutavadha)

diseases.description: Scabies or inflammatory condition in the anus of infants. New specific entry in Volume 2.
Bronchial asthma in children. Volume 2 lists Dhanyaka as the primary herb.
Seizures and convulsive disorders in children caused by various grahas (entities). Lists Ajagandha, Aralu and Asphota.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Seizures in children causing various syndromes (Grahavadha, Bhutavadha)
A vatic-disorder characterised by fits of convulsions with loss of consciousness

diseases.description: Severe malnutrition and wasting in infants (marasmus). Single herb — Asvagandha, the premier tonic for building body mass.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Excessive hunger and digestion causing loss of dhatus, emaciation and debility
Promoting body strength; muscular strength; resistance to diseases; tonic

diseases.description: Ophthalmia neonatorum; inflammation of the eye in the new-born child. Single herb — Jambu.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Ophthalmia neonatorum; characterised by inflammation of eye in new-born child

diseases.description: Cough in children. Single herb — Dhanyaka (coriander), a mild respiratory herb safe for children.
Intestinal or digestive malabsorption in children. Single herb — Jambu.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Disorders of Grahani organ; malabsorption syndrome; chronic amoebiasis/colitis

diseases.description: Inflammation of the umbilicus in newborns (omphalitis). Single herb — Candana (sandalwood) for its anti-infective and cooling properties.
Post-procedural care herbs after ritual earlobes piercing. Single herb — Pancavalkala (five-bark combination) for wound healing and antisepsis.
Herbs for promoting elongation and healthy growth of earlobes (a classical practice of beauty and auspiciousness). Single herb — Gunja.
Inflammation of rectal lining. Single herb — Daruharidra (Indian barberry) for its anti-infective and anti-inflammatory properties.
Systematic rejuvenation therapy to restore youth, vitality and longevity. Volume 2 lists Madhuka and Mamsi.
Special category of Rasayana herbs specifically promoting memory, intellect and cognitive function. Volume 2 adds Matsyaksi to the classical brain tonic group.

Swollen rectal or anal veins. Volume 2 is the most comprehensive formulation — 38 herbs including Kantakari, Kapittha, Kola, Kovidara, Kulattha, Kusa, Langali, Lonika, Madhuka, Mahanimba, Mamsi and Manjistha.
Haemorrhoidal bleeding with bright red rectal blood loss. Volume 2 adds Cukrika, Dukrika and Durva.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Intrinsic haemorrhage due to vitiation of blood and bile

diseases.description: Fatal viral neurological infection from animal bite. Volume 2 adds Jalavetasa, Kakodumbara and Nala.
Food or contact poisoning from rat toxins. Volume 2 adds Kakadani, Kakamaci and Kosataki.
Venomous scorpion sting requiring emergency treatment. Volume 2 adds Jayanti, Karpasa and Kasamarda.
Venomous snakebite management. Volume 2 adds Dravanti, Girikarnika, Harenuka, Kakajangha, Kovidara, Kustha, Lajjalu, Manjistha, Mayura-Sikha and Nakuli.
Venomous spider bite toxicity. Volume 2 lists Arkaparni, Hribera and Karpasa.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Indicated, useful in and countering spider-bite poisoning effect

diseases.description: Viral eruptive febrile illness with skin pustules. Volume 2 adds Gavedhuka, Hilamocika, Jambira, Juya, Kancanara, Khadira, Karavellaka and Matulunga.

Group of 20 urinary disorders characterised by increased turbid urine including diabetes. Volume 2 adds Kampillaka, Kataka, Khadira, Ksirivrksa, Kusumbha, Kutaja, Madayanti, Mahanimba, Manjistha, Mocarasa and Mustaka.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: A group of diseases with anomalies of urine with increased frequency and turbidity

diseases.description: Sugar in urine (glycosuria) — a subtype of Prameha with sweet-tasting urine like sugarcane juice. Single herb — Jaya.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: A group of diseases with anomalies of urine

diseases.description: Diabetes mellitus — the honey-urine type of Prameha with sweet turbid urine. Volume 2 specifically lists Kadara, Jambu, Bilva, Bimbi, Mesasrngi, Methika and Karavellaka.
Semen in urine; a subtype of Prameha. Single herb — Arjuna.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: A group of diseases with anomalies of urine

diseases.description: Protrusion of rectal mucosa through the anus. Volume 2 lists Amlika, Cangeri, Kamala and Karavellaka.
Therapeutic purgation (Virecana karma) to eliminate Pitta and toxins through the intestines. Volume 2 lists Arka, Danti, Karavellaka and Krsnabija.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Purification; radical elimination of morbid substances

diseases.description: Internal bleeding from vitiation of blood and bile — bleeding from multiple orifices. Volume 2 adds Anjira, Atimuktaka, Ingudi, Jambu, Laja, Kakodumbara, Kamala, Kasmarya, Kovidara, Kumuda, Lodhra, Madayanti, Mallika, Mocarasa and Mudga.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Intrinsic haemorrhage due to vitiation of rakta (blood) and pitta (bile)

diseases.description: Complete Rasayana formulation list from Volume 2 — the most extensive rejuvenation herb collection. Adds Copacini-dvipantaravaca, Dhava, Haimavati vaca and Hastikarna to the core group.
Restoration of skin pigmentation in vitiligo, leucoderma and hypopigmentation. Volume 2 lists Bakuci and Bhallataka.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Useful in promoting complexion of the skin (pigmentation)

diseases.description: Inability to pass urine; urinary retention. Volume 2 lists Darbha, Draksa, Duralabha and Haritaki.
Abnormal scrotal enlargement (hydrocele or orchitis). Volume 2 adds Indravaruni, Jaya, Kakadani, Kosamra, Lajjalu, Madhuka and Nakuli.
Abnormal sinus tract or fistula in nasal or body tissue. Volume 2 adds Cancu, Karanja, Karcura, Kodrava, Kumbhika, Mocarasa, Nirgundi and Jati.
General category of skin diseases. Volume 2 adds Cakramarda, Dusrava, Bakuci, Khadira, Kutaja and Nimba.

associated_sanskrit_terms.meaning: Promoting skin health; palliative for skin diseases
